la:noun:ripa.html:
rīpa, ae, f.
etym. dub.; cf. rivus
,
the bank of a stream (while litus is the coast, shore of the sea; v. Döderl. Syn. Part. 3, p. 208; freq. and class. in sing. and plur.), Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 41 Vahl.): ripas radentia flumina rodunt,: ex utrāque parte ripae fluminis,: Romulus urbem perennis amnis posuit in ripā,; : viridissima gramine ripa,: turba ad ripas effusa ruebat,: umbrosa,: declivis,; .— Comically: ripis superat mihi atque abundat pectus laetitiā meum,: vos mihi amnes estis, vestrā ripā vos sequar,.—
Transf., the shore of the sea: villa semper mare recte conspicit ... numquam ex ripā, sed haud paulum submota a litore (sc. respergitur), never (immediately) from the bank, but (rather) a good way back from the shore, : sentiant ... Aequoris nigri fremitum, et trementes Verbere ripas, : maris ripa,; .

la:adj:ridiculus.html:
rīdĭcŭlus, a, um, adj.
rideo
,
that excites laughter.
In a good sense, laughable, droll, funny, amusing, facetious (freq. and class.; syn.: jocularis, jocosus).
Adj.: quamvis ridiculus est,; cf.: quando adbibero, alludiabo, tum sum ridiculissimus,: si ridiculum hominem quaeret quispiam,: cavillator facie magis quam facetiis ridiculus,: homines,; ; : mus,a funny little mouse,: inest lepos ludusque in hac comoediā: ridicula res est,: ridicula et jocosa res, and 4: dico unum ridiculum dictum de dictis melioribus . . . nemo ridet,; so, dictum,: logos ridiculos vendo,: vultus gestusque, et saep.: ridiculum est, with subject-clause: ridiculum est, te istuc me admonere,; so .— Absol.: hui, tam cito? ridiculum!how comical!; so ; ; .— Poet. with inf.: (Porcius) Ridiculus totas simul obsorbere placentas,.—
Substt.
rīdĭcŭ-lus, i, m., a jester, buffoon: Gelasimo nomen mihi indidit parvo pater. Quia inde jam a pauxillo puero ridiculus fui, etc.,; so and 64;

4, 2, 54; ; ; ; .—

rīdĭcŭlum, i, or plur.: rīdĭcŭla, ōrum, n., something laughable, a laughing matter; a jest, joke, etc.: proprium materiae, de quā nunc loquimur, est ridiculum, ideoque haec tota disputatio a Graecis περὶ γελοίου inscribitur, ; cf. (v. the whole chapter on laughter, when and how it should be excited, etc., Cic. l. l.; and: de risu,): in jaciendo mittendoque ridiculo genera plura sunt ... illud admonemus, ridiculo sic usurum oratorem, ut, etc.,: per ridiculum dicere (opp. severe),: ridiculi causā (with joco),: mihi solae ridiculo fuit,I had the joke all to myself,: quatenus sint ridicula tractanda oratori, perquam diligenter videndum est ... materies omnis ridiculorum est in istis vitiis, quae, etc.,; : saepe etiam sententiose ridicula dicuntur,: facetum non tantum circa ridicula consistere,: ridicula aut facimus aut dicimus, etc.,.—
In a bad sense, laughable, silly, absurd, ridiculous (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; cf. rideo, II. B. 2.): hujus insania, quae ridiaula est aliis, mihi tum molesta sane fuit, etc.,: ludibria,: qui ridiculus minus illo (es)?: stulta reprehendere facillimum est, nam per se sunt ridicula,; cf. (with stulta),: poëma (shortly before: inculti versus et male nati),: pudor,.— Ridiculum est, with subject-clause: est ridiculum, ad ea quae habemus nihil dicere, quaerere, quae habere non possumus,; so, putare,: de confessis praecipere,.—Adv.: rīdĭ-cŭlē.
(Acc. to I.) Laughably, jokingly, humorously: rogitas,; : non modo acute, sed etiam ridicule ac facete,; ; ; Domit. Mars. ap. : ridicule magis hoc dictum quam vere,.—
(Acc. to II.) Ridiculously: insanus,; .

la:noun:rima.html:
rīma, ae, f.
for rigma, from rig, ringor; hence, that gapes, yawns
,
a cleft, crack, chink, fissure (cf. hiatus): angusta,: cava,: patet,; cf. hiscit,: tabernae rimas agunt,are cracked,; so, rimas agere,; ; and in a like sense, ducere,: facere,to make,: explere, to stop up, Cic, Or. 69, 231; cf.: nec te signata juvabunt Limina, persuasae fallere rima sat est,—
= cunnus, .— Poet.: ignea rima micans, i. e. a flash of lightning (qs. cleaving the sky), ; imitated by ,

§ 112.—

Transf., comically: plenus rimarum sum: hac atque hac perfluo, I am full of chinks, i. e. can keep nothing to myself, conceal nothing, (opp. tacere, continere); .

la:verb:rideo.html:
rīdĕo, si, sum, 2 (
dep. collat. form ridetur, ; ), v. n. and a. [Bœot. κριδδέμεν for κρίζειν?͂ γελᾶν, orig. form κριδjεμεν].
Neutr., to laugh (cf. cachinnor).
In gen.: numquam ullo die risi adaeque Neque hoc quod reliquom est plus risuram opinor,: risi te hodie multum,: ridere convivae, cachinnare ipse Apronius,: M. Crassum semel ait in vitā risisse Lucilius,: cum ridere voles,.—With si: ridetque (deus), si mortalis ultra Fas trepidat. ; so ; ; : ridentem dicere verum Quid vetat, while laughing, i. e. in a laughing or jesting manner, ; cf. .—With a homogeneous object: ridere γέλωτα σαρδάνιον, : tempus flendi et tempus ridendi,.—
In partic.
To laugh pleasantly, to smile; and ridere ad aliquem or alicui, to smile on one (so almost entirely poet.; syn. renideo): Juppiter hic risit tempestatesque serenae Riserunt omnes risu Jovis omnipotentis, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 445 sq. Vahl.); cf.: vultu Fortuna sereno,: ridere ad patrem,.—
Transf., of things, to laugh or smile, i. q. to look cheerful or pleasant: sedes quietae large diffuso lumine rident,: tempestas,: argentum et pulchra Sicyonia,: ille terrarum mihi praeter omnes Angulus ridet,: argento domus,: florum coloribus almus ager,: pavonum ridenti lepore,; cf.: colocasia mixta ridenti acantho, smiling, i. e. glad, . — With dat.: tibi rident aequora ponti,smile upon thee, look brightly up to thee,; . — *
To laugh in ridicule, to mock (cf. II. B. 2.): quandoque potentior Largis muneribus riserit aemuli,.—
Act., to laugh at, laugh over any thing.
In gen. (class.; cf. Brix ad ): rideo hunc,; cf. : Acrisium (Juppiter et Venus), et saep.: risi nivem atram,: joca tua,: haec ego non rideo, quamvis tu rideas,say in jest,: nemo illic vitia ridet,; cf.: perjuria amantum (Juppiter), ; ; for which: perjuros amantes, (3, 8), 47.—Poet., with obj.-clause: Amphitryoniaden perdere Sidonios umeris amictus,. — Pass.: haec enim ridentur vel sola vel maxime, quae notant et designant turpitudinem aliquam non turpiter, etc.,: tum enim non sal, sed natura ridetur,. 69, 279; 2, 70, 281: ridetur ab omni Conventu,: ridear,: neque acute tantum ac venuste, sed stulte, iracunde, timide dicta aut facta ridentur,: quae in mimis rideri solent,.—
In partic.
To smile upon one: quasi muti silent Neque me rident,; cf.: cui non risere parentes,.—
To laugh at, ridicule a person or thing (milder than deridere, to deride): ridet nostram amentiam,: O rem, quam homines soluti ridere non desinant,: ut dederis nobis quemadmodum scripseris ad me, quem semper ridere possemus,; cf.: curre et quam primum haec risum veni,: versus Enni gravitate minores (with reprehendere),: risimus et merito nuper poëtam,: nostram diligentiam,: praesaga Verba senis (with spernere),: lacrimas manus impia nostras, al.—Pass.: Pyrrhi ridetur largitas a consule,: rideatur merito, qui, etc.,; cf. ; ; : rideri possit eo, quod, etc.,: peccet ad extremum ridendus,; cf. ; .
la:verb:rideo.inflection: si, sum, 2, v. n. and a.

la:noun:risus.html:
rīsus, ūs, m.
id.
,
a laughing, laughter, laugh (equally freq. in sing. and plur.): risum movere ... quid sit risus,; cf. the whole chapter, De risu,: alicui risum magis quam stomachum movere,; cf.: risum judicis movere,: risus populi factus est,; cf.: risus facere, Cael. ap. : miros risus nos edere, (10), 2; for which: ne spissae risum tollant coronae,: risus captare,; so, risum captare,; : mediocris quidam est risus consecutus non in te, sed, etc.,: in eam tabulam magni risus consequebantur,: togam sum ejus magno hominum risu cavillatus, (12), 2: risu cognoscere matrem,: amara lento Temperet risu,: proditor Gratus puellae risus,; : risui sorori fuit,; ; : nimis aegre risum continui,: nequeo risu me admoderarier,: risu emoriri,: risu clandestino rumpier, Afran. ap. : unde oriebantur risus dulcesque cachinni,: paene ille timore, ego risu corrui, (10), 2.—
Transf., an object of laughter: deus omnibus risus erat,.—
A jest, a practical joke, mockery: qui per jocum deos inridens, jussit, etc.... qui risus populo cladem attulit,.—
Personified, as a deity, .

senses: alternative form of rīdeō (“to laugh”) (attested in Hilarius and Diomedes)

rīpŭla, ae, f.dim.
ripa

la:noun:rixa.gloss: quarrel, brawl, dispute, contest, strife, contention
senses: quarrel, brawl, dispute, contest, strife, contention
la:noun:rixa.html:
rixa, ae, f.
perh. root rig, whence ringor; the suffix -sa like noxa from noc-eo; hence, prop., the wide opening of the mouth
.
A quarrel, brawl, dispute, contest, strife, contention (class.; esp. freq. after the Aug. period; syn.: contentio, altercatio, disceptatio, jurgium): ecce nova turba atque rixa,: rixa ac prope proelium fuit,: rixa sedata est,: in rixā esse,: in rixam ire,: sive geris jocos Seu rixam et insanos amores,: rixa super mero Debellata,: Academiae nostrae cum Zenone magna rixa est,: pietatis rixa,: jurgia primum, mox rixa,.—Plur.: corrupta jurgiis aut rixis disciplina,: crebrae,: sanguineae,: immodicae,.—Prov.: a lasso rixam quaeri, v. lassus.—
In gen., a battle, contest (very rare): major cum Oceano quam cum ipsis navibus rixa,. — Of beasts: deque tuo fiet ... Insatiabilibus corpore rixa lupis,; ; .

la:adv:rite.gloss: according to religious usage, with due observances, with proper ceremonies, ceremonially, solemnly, duly
senses: according to religious usage, with due observances, with proper ceremonies, ceremonially, solemnly, duly
la:adv:rite.html:
rītĕ, adv.
perh. an old abl. form collat. with ritu, as, on the other hand, diu with die, and noctu with nocte; subst. rite = ritu, is now found only in rite nefasto libatus,
.
Lit., according to religious ceremonies or observances; and pregn., with due religious observances or rites, according to religious usage: nocturna mulierum sacrificia ne sunto praeter olla quae pro populo rite fient,: rite veteres, rite etiam vestri coluere divos, id. poët. Div. 1, 13, 21: neque duobus nisi certis deis rite una hostia fieri,: exsequiis rite solutis,: centum mactabat rite bidentes,: deos apprecati,: Latonae puerum canentes,: rebus divinis perpetratis,: pecora sacrificant,: votum solvi,: templa sacerdotum rite dicata manu,.—
Transf., in gen., in a proper or just manner; fitly, duly, rightly, aright, well: quod fit rite id ratum ac rectum est, Müll.: rite significat bene ac recte, Paul. ex ib.: idque ut rite intellegas te facere, Afran. ap. P.: hunc deum rite beatum dixerimus, rightly, with justice or reason, ; so, habere,: appellari,; ; : creatus tribunus,: rebus paratis,: memor,: aperire partus,: mens rite Nutrita,: si maxima Juno Rite vocor,; : QVON RITE RECTE DE FINIBVS CVM VELIENS. ACTVM SIT,: deos veneror, Ut, quod de meā re huc veni, rite venerim,at the right time, fortunately,; : Nymphas venerabar, Rite secundarent visus,.—
In the usual way, manner, or fashion; according to custom or usage: retinentes pocula rite,: campestres Scythae, Quorum plaustra vagas rite trahunt domos,: religatos rite videbat Carpere gramen equos,. —
Esp., in the manner or form prescribed by law, legally, formally, solemnly: hic enim rite productust patri,: rite creatus tribunus,: matrimonium rite confectum,.

la:noun:rivus.gloss: a small stream (of water); brook, stream, rivulet
senses: a small stream (of water); brook, stream, rivulet
an artificial watercourse; channel, conduit, canal
la:noun:rivus.html:
rīvus, i, m.
root ri- (li-), to flow, drop; Gr. λίμνη; cf. liris; Sanscr. rīna, flowing; cf. ripa
,
a small stream of water, a brook (cf.: fluvius, amnis).
Lit.: rivus est locus per longitudinem depressus, quo aqua decurrat, cui nomen est ἀπὸ τοῦ ῥεῖν, (de rivis), 1: rivorum a fonte deductio,: prostrati in gramine molli Propter aquae rivum,by a waterbrook,; so, aquae,; ; cf. : omnia flumina atque omnes rivos, qui ad mare pertinebant, etc.,; ; cf. 3, 88 fin.; : pronus,; : mobiles,; cf. celeres,: gelidi,; : claudite jam rivos,: tenuis fugiens per gramina rivus,.—Prov.: e rivo flumina magna facere, to magnify an insignificant object; or, as we say, to make a mountain of a mole-hill, .—
Transf.
An artificial water-course, channel, canal, ; ; .—
A gutter, (7), 1 al.—
Of other liquids, a stream, etc. (mostly poet.): manabat venis ferventibus argenti rivus et auri,: lactis uberes,: sanguinis,; ; : sudoris,: lacrimarum,: ignium,: rivis currentia vina,.—
Trop., a stream (very rare; v. rivulus, II.): liquidus fortunae rivus,: facundiae rivus, Lact. Opif. Dei, 20 fin.

la:verb:rigo.gloss: to irrigate, to lead, convey or conduct (a liquid to a place)
senses: to irrigate, to lead, convey or conduct (a liquid to a place)
to wet, moisten, water or bedew something with a liquid; suckle; bathe
la:verb:rigo.html:
rĭgoāvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
cf. Gr. βρέχω, to wet; Germ. Regen, rain
.
To wet, moisten, water, bedew any thing with a liquid (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: irrigo, madefacio).
Lit.: imbres omnia maria ac terras sparguntque rigantque,: Nilus rigat Aegyptum,; (for which, irrigat, ); so, prata (fons),; ; cf.: lucum perenni aquā (fons). : campos (Euphratis) accolae,: arbores,; cf. seminaria (opp. conspergere),: quā Tanais Getas rigat,: lacrimis ora,: fletibus ora, ; ; ; ; —Absol.: nubes nimbique rigantes,; so, accolae,.—
Poet., transf.: natos vitali rore, i. e. to suckle, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 12, 20: solis uti lux ac vapor cernuntur terras rigare,bedew, flood,; cf. : Babylonica, to wet (sc. with urine), .—
Trop., to water, bedew, etc.: omnium ingenia,: ora alicujus Philetaeā aquā, .—
Like irrigo, to lead, convey, or conduct water or any other liquid to a place (very rare).
Lit.: aquam Albanam emissam per agros rigabis (= ad rigandum diduces), an old oracle in Drak. N. cr.: vitalem sanguinem per venas,. —
Trop.: hinc motus per membra rigantur,are directed, conveyed,: somnum per pectora, Furius ap. (for which, irrigat, ; ).

la:verb:rigeo.gloss: to be stiff or numb; stiffen
senses: to be stiff or numb; stiffen
to stand upright; stand on end
la:verb:rigeo.html:
rĭgĕo, ēre, v. n.
prob. kindr. with ῥιγέω, frigeo
,
to be stiff or numb; to stiffen (syn.: concresco, conglacio).
Lit. (class.).
With cold: frigore,; (opp. uri calore): gelu,; ; : prata rigent,: stagnum,: corpora omnibus,; cf. poet.: horridus December,.—
Of any physical stiffness: gelido comae terrore rigebant,stood on end, bristled up,; so, ora indurata,: ardua cervix (with horrent setae),: cerealia dona rigent,i. e. are hardened into gold,: vestes auroque ostroque,are stiff, stand out,; cf.: terga boum plumbo insuto ferroque,: manicae ex auro,: signa,.—
Poet., transf., to stand stiff or upright: (pars summa scopuli) riget,; : late riget Tmolus,: sine frondibus arbos,: illitterati num minus nervi rigent?.—
Trop., to remain unmoved, inert (very rare): feritas immota riget,. —Hence, rĭgens, entis, P. a., stiff, inflexible, rigid, unbending (mostly post-class.).
Lit.: secui madidas ungue rigente genas,: lorica ex aere,: aqua,i. e. frozen,: pars mundi ipsis aquilonis conceptaculis rigentissima,: caput (with praedurum),rigid,; cf. : interque rigentes (partes terrae), : gelu flumina,.—
Trop., stubborn, inflexible, unyielding: animus,; cf.: vir tot malis,.

la:adj:rimosus.gloss: full of cracks, chinks, or fissures; cracked
senses: full of cracks, chinks, or fissures; cracked
la:adj:rimosus.html:
rīmōsus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
full of cracks, chinks, or fissures (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: fores, (3, 9), 16: cymba,: aedificium (with fissum),: vasa,.— Comp.: pulmo,.—
Trop.: quae rimosā bene deponuntur in aure,i. e. that keeps nothing secret,: nihil in eā (animā) rimosum est ac remissum,.

la:verb:rimor.html:
rīmor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. [rima].
Orig. belonging to agricultural lang., to lay open, tear up, turn up the ground: rastris terram rimantur,.— Of animals, to root up, turn up, grub through: volucres rimantur prata Caystri,: stagna et paludes (volucres),: paludem (sues),.—
Transf., to tear up, turn over insearch of any thing; to pry into, search, examine, explore (not freq. till after the Aug. per.).
Lit.: vultur Viscera rimatur epulis,rummages for food,: haruspex Pectora pullorum rimatur et exta catelli,: humum pilis et lanceis,: partes rimatur apertas, Qua vulnus letale ferat,: oculis caeli plagas, Varr. ap. ; ; cf.: elatis naribus auras,; cf.: rimatus fustem cunctis vastiorem,.— Absol.: quod cuique repertum Rimanti,. —
Trop., to examine thoroughly, investigate (syn.: scrutor, investigo, indago): hanc quidem rationem naturae difficile est fortasse traducere ad id genus divinationis; sed tamen id quoque rimatur quantum potest, Posidonius (the figure taken from the haruspices or augurs), * : mihi cuncta rimanti,; cf. ; : secreta,: metus ejus,: offensas,—
To find out, comprehend: ego autem rimari non queo, unde hoc sit, etc.,.?*!
Act. collat. form, rīmo, āre, Att. ap. ; Poët. ap. Fest. s. v. ruspari, p. 265 Müll.; cf. P.—
rī-mātus, a, um, pass., .

la:noun:ritus.html:
rītus, ūs (
gen. rituis, Varr. ap. ; abl. rite nefasto, ; v. rite), m.
etym. unknown
, orig. belonging to relig. lang.
Lit., the form and manner of religious observances; a religious usage or ceremony, a rite (cf. caerimonia): Graeco ritu sacra non Romano facere, Müll.: sacra diis aliis Albano ritu, Graeco Herculi facit,: quo haec privatim et publice modo rituque flant, discunto ignari a publicis sacerdotibus,; cf.: morem ritusque sacrorum Adiciam,: de more rituque priscae religionis,: ex patriis ritibus optuma colunto,; : tempestates, quae populi Romani ritibus consecratae sunt,: regina dei (sc. Bacchi) Ritibus instruitur,: sacrificos docuit ritus,: profanos ritus exuere,: lustrari magico ritu,.—
Transf., in gen., a custom, usage, manner, mode, way: ritus, mos vel consuetudo, Müll.; cf. ib.
Usually in abl. sing. and with a foll. gen., after the usage, wont, manner, or fashion of any thing.
With gen.: more ferarum Quadrupedumque ritu,: qui pecudum ritu ad voluptatem omnia referunt,: pecudum, ferarumque,; ; ; ; : latronum vivere,: juvenum,: Lucili,: Herculis (petiisse laurum),; cf. Dianae (cincta, etc.),; ; : fluminis,: tempestatis,: non hominis sed accipitris,: volucri ritu flammarum,.—
With adj.: haec mulier cantherino ritu astans somniat,: ritu barbarico esse,: res quaeque suo ritu procedit,: novo Sublime moliar atrium,: aleatorio,; cf.: rancida quo perolent projecta cadavera ritu,in the way that, such as,.—
In other cases (mostly poet. and post-Aug.), habit, custom, usage: cognosse Sabinae Gentis ritus,: referre Cyclopum,: humanos,: in alienos ritus mores legesque verti,: ritus dissimiles habuere duo examina apium,: moresque tractamus innumeros,: externas caerimonias, Aegyptios Judiacosque ritus compescuit,; : de ritu nuptiarum,.

la:adj:rigidus.html:
rĭgĭdus, a, um, adj.
rigeo
,
stiff, hard, inflexible, rigid (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose; cf. durus).
Lit.: pruinae,; cf.: rigidum permanat frigus ad ossa,: tellus,: aqua,: umbrae,: frigus,: cervicem rectam oportet esse non rigidam aut supinam,; cf. ; so, cervix,; ; : artus morte,: crura,: rostrum,: cornu,: setae,: capilli,: oculi (with extenti), et saep.: quercus,; cf. columnae,: malus,.— In mal. part.: illud,; cf. .— Hence: custos ruris,i. e. Priapus,; ; and absol.: rĭgĭda, f., : silices,hard,; : saxum,: mons,hard, rocky,: Niphates,: ferrum,: serae,: ensis,; : hasta,: unguis, et saep.—
